item.title: Another product of The Factory
item.description: Table settings that put themselves back where they belong
item.content:encoded:
It's a set of six simple table settings in boxes. If you take a piece (like a fork or a plate) out of the box and set it on a table, it locks onto that position. If you move it somewhere else and leave it alone for an hour, it will go back to where it belongs. If you sufficiently destroy the table, the pieces will return to their original boxes.

This is a very simple, old-school, "normal thing with a gimmick" kind of idea. Has it been done before? How can I make an article about this more fun and interesting? Is this just a bad or boring idea? All feedback and questions are appreciated! :-)

item.title: [Seeking Greenlights]Retribution Gun
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a BB toy gun. When someone shoots the gun at someone else, the person who has been shot will show high levels of hostility towards the shooter, and try to take SCP-XXXX from the shooter. If the person that has been shot manages to retrieve the gun from the shooter, he or she will shoot it at the person who shot first, and in this case an actual bullet will be fired instead of a BB toy bullet, killing the initial shooter. The second shooter will then lose consciousness.

Central Narrative: The gun was taken from a crime scene where a 10-yo boy killed his friend while playing with toy guns, one of which was SCP-XXXX.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I tried to keep it an idea that doesn't have a lot yet still presentable. Its anomalous properties are clear and simple.

item.title: suadeant (seeking greenlights)
item.description: A symbiotic, disembodied voice which can be very... suggestive.
item.content:encoded:
Hello! This is my first attempt to get reviewed on anything so forgive me if it's not quite the correct format!

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Other (paradoxical)

Elevator Pitch: So it is thought to be a telepathic entity as the "voice" is never recorded, though it is "heard". Sometimes it is "seen" however, witness accounts differ so much it is not clear whether there are multiple entities, it changes appearance, or the witnesses are subject to a form of hysteria "if you stare into a dark room ling enough, you will eventually see something"

My thought is that the entity gets some form of nourishment by it's host acting counter to their normal behavior and it is even more valuable if the host doesn't acknowledge the entity's existance at all. Denial of its existance is good, but not as good as complete ignorance.

Central Narrative: It needs to be visited each day and the subject must remain with the entity long enough to confirm that it is in fact still contained. There is a real danger of the entity escaping sue to its nature of wanting to be forgotten, and it may have been once or twice and had it's containment treated as an "empty" chamber, allowing it to escape.

To contain, the entity will be visited by a subject each day.
The subject will be given a myriad of monotonous tasks to be completed with a large amount of inocuous restrictions placed on them. The reasoning is to give the entity a large amount of non-dangerous things to tempt the subject with and avoid another D-508905 incident.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: "something that thrives by convincing it's host that it does not exist."

Additional Notes: I figure that it will operate within the confines of suggestions available. Starting off small, but desiring a much larger payoff when available. Biding it's time while it "grooms" it's host into more severe self-contradictions.

I imagine Euclid for it's classification.

Please tell me what you think :) i hope i can start being a real contributer soon! ^^

item.title: SCP-XXXX: Empathic Erhu (seeking greenlights)
item.description: A musical instrument that creates instantaneous empathy
item.content:encoded:
A musical instrument that creates instantaneous empathy, and the ethical/philosophical conflicts within the Foundation that result from it.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mythological, Philosophical

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP layout with some tests and a few cross-tests

Elevator Pitch:

  • SCP-XXXX is an emotokinetic1 erhu that when played causes anyone who hears it to receive all of the emotions and underlying memories of the player.
  • SCP-XXXX achieves this "instantaneous empathy" by generating empathons, the elementary subatomic particle of the psychospace responsible for human emotion.2
  • SCP-XXXX can transmit any human emotion, resulting in a conflict between the O5 Council and the Ethics Committee concerning how best to use SCP-XXXX.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is hand-delivered to the Foundation by the headless god of perseverance Xíng Tiān, who says that it will help humanity by bringing individuals together. Testing reveals that SCP-XXXX does this by using empathons to broadcast the emotions of the person playing SCP-XXXX.

+ show block
– hide block

However, because SCP-XXXX can use empathons to transmit any human emotion, a conflict arises between the O-5 Council, who want to weaponize SCP-XXXX, and the Ethics Committee, who want to use SCP-XXXX as a mode of communication with sapient SCP's.

This conflict is resolved when Xíng Tiān hijacks SCP-XXXX and gives all the D-class at Site-64 the ability to emotokinetically communicate with each other, allowing them to cooperate and pool their knowledge of certain SCP's to coordinate a prison break that leads to the loss of several SCP personnel.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX is an anomalous musical instrument that generates instantaneous empathy, and this emotokinetic ability results in an ethical conflict within the Foundation. SCP-XXXX also expands upon the lore of the psychospace and certain humanoid SCP's such as SCP-5027 and SCP-5278.

Additional Notes:

  • I know that Series I SCP's like SCP-187 and SCP-682 are fairly overdone; I would be happy to substitute them for more recent SCP's. Essentially, I need an SCP with precognitive abilities and an SCP that's physically invincible.
  • I read SCP-5027 a few weeks ago and loved the premise, although I did get bummed out by the ending. If the author of SCP-5027 is okay with it, I would like to use SCP-XXXX to give SCP-5027 a somewhat happier ending (nothing like leaving containment, but at least an ending where SCP-5027 can be treated like a human being).
  • Lastly, thank you for reading this SCP idea! Any guidance is much appreciated, and I look forward to hearing from you!

Collapsible edited as the post was still rather long. ~Zyn

Footnotes
1. capable of controlling the emotions of sentient beings
2. similar to the Higgs Boson being responsible for mass or the photon being responsible for light

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] Unsolved Hypercube
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a Rubik's cube which, when close to being solved, begins to behave like a 4-dimensional Rubik's cube to prevent itself from being solved. When it nears being solved again it will instead begin to behave like a 5-dimensional Rubik's cube, and so on. After being far away enough from being solved it will revert to a lower dimension. These processes have a consistent order and pattern. As a byproduct SCP-XXXXs mass increases with each dimension over 3 dimensions it contains (starting with the mass of a regular Rubik's cube) as well as giving off a small amount of ionizing radiation. This increase in mass and the presence of radiation grows exponentially with each additional dimension.

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this piece would take the form of several testing logs where Dr. Cass experiments with SCP-XXXX and its unusual properties. Over time they work towards the possibility of using SCP-XXXXs radioactive properties for fuel in a power generator based on fusion reactor designs. This pursuit eventually leads to conflict with the site director who is against the idea. By the end of it the site director removes Dr. Cliff as the project lead (instead having them as a project advisor) and further experimentation with SCP-XXXX is delayed until a new project lead can be established.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The primary hook of this article is the mundane appearance of the anomaly in question. As people read it some might look at a Rubik’s cube they have (or a memory of it) which can draw them in closer. It's also a simple concept (a Rubik’s cube which prevents you from solving it) but goes very deep into the mechanics of the anomaly and such a concept actually works.

Additional Notes: None.

item.title: Super Turbo Laser Motorcarriage
item.description: A particularly dangerous MK II Toyota Supra
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-Fi

Page Layout (Optional): I'm planning to add, to the usual stuff, a short log of the manhunt, three interviews with the driver and a test log - in that order.

Elevator Pitch: A MK II Supra. The faster it goes, the more universally degrading/degenerative its shell becomes - to the point where it can cut clean through practically anything. As a trade-off, it loses speed proportionally to damage done.

Central Narrative:
+ Central Narrative
- Hide

From the American midwest and moving south, a retired stuntman drives recklessly and attracts the police. In chases, he uses the car to his advantage - cutting through roadblocks and anything else that stands in his way. The Foundation is, of course, not very fond of this, and teams up with the FBI for a manhunt, which lasts 2 whole days and ultimately ends with a cleverly placed spike strip.

The old man is then brought in in a heavily intoxicated state, high on cocaine and MDMA. The three separate interviews are conducted within 1, 3 and 7 days inside his padded holding cell, which reveal the man's motivation to be a combination of forced retirement, an uneventful lifestyle and poverty. The straw that broke the camel's back was the death of his only friend, whose will provided him with the built black-on-yellow car. Realizing his life is already lived and not going to get better, the old man is overcome by rage and sadness. In that moment, he snaps and decides to go out with a bang - by buying copious amounts of drugs and embarking on a journey to the Californian West Coast, where he had once spent the brightest days of his youth.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The old man's story and interviews with a side serving of experiments conducted on the car.

Additional Notes: I'm debating, whether or not I should make the car's abilities wane over time as per active use.

The old man's friend knew of the anomalous properties, and kept it locked up in a rented garage out of fear and paranoia.

The car was first found left in the middle of his car lot one night.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] SCP article
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: yes

Page type: SCP article

Elevator pitch: SCP that steals the conscousness of random people, leaving their body on autopilot whilst their consciousness is put in a state of terror.

Central narrative: SCP-XXXX is an entity composed of a human head with oblong arms extending from where the ears should be. SCP-XXXX steals the victims consciousness for ascending time increments.

The victim’s body acts on “autopilot”, going about the day as normal. However, the body avoids conversation as much as possible and will simplify tasks to the furthest extent. For example, the body will make lunch for itself, but only the barest needs ie. It will take an apple and bottle of water instead of making use of an oven or stove.

It is unclear what happens to the consciousness when in SCP-XXXX’s control, as all memory is erased once the consciousness returns. However, once the consciousness has returned, the victim will feel large discomfort and disorientation at not being where they last remember being.

SCP-XXXX is found after having a researcher targeted by it. Suddenly the researcher stops taking notes during an SCP observation and simply sits and watches. After 5 minutes, they return to normal although slightly disorientated. This happens again during lunch the following day, the researcher finishes their food and simply sits and stares ahead. This is noted by foundation personnel and investigation goes into discovering that this is the work of the entity.

Hook: Attempts at communication show the entity to be slightly smarter than the average human. The creature claims to only want to show its victims what life could be like without having limitations in its realm of dreams. However, once subjects are exposed to the entity for extended periods, their body starts to meld with the floor until they cease existing altogether, from the minds of everyone. The only proof that they ever existed is written and video proof.

Additional notes: I am worried that this is very similar to other SCP’s like SCP 2774. How would I go about making it vastly different or making it an alternate version that can be communicated with? Any critique will be helpful as well as suggestions on what to change.

item.title: SCP "Darkhouse" - [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Terminal / SCP Historical

Page Layout (Optional): Discovery (audio recordings; scanned original documents; terminal)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Perhaps there was a reason why the O5-Council decided to bury this information…

Elevator Pitch:
+ Open
- Close

A Junior Researcher logs onto an older terminal and uncovers a forgotten SCP with deep roots in the SCP foundations history.


Central Narrative:
+ Open
- Close

The SCP foundation has a questionable history, but this Junior Researcher attempts to solidify one of the oldest SCPs discovered by the Foundation. Compiling information from older terminals and transcribing paper archives, the SCP “Darkhouse” is reclassified as one of the earliest discovered SCPs. The SCP was “lost” when the Foundation transferred their data from paper to computers.

Dating back to 1792, the original Cape Henry Lighthouse was the first federally funded public works project of the newly formed United States government. In 1881, a new lighthouse was constructed to replace the original. With rising threats from around the world, both human and anomalous, the United States government attempted to utilize unexplainable properties the original lighthouse possessed.

The SCP “Darkhouse” ‘s anomalous properties are charged by UVA (315-400 nm) and UVB (280-315 nm) Ultraviolet radiation. The radiation appears to activate the anomalous properties, causing the SCP “Darkhouse” to enter an “active” state. During this state, the SCP “Darkhouse” will project a photon-absorbing substance, blocking all light it encompasses. Effects of the substance on living organisms have been redacted due to its tendencies to dissolve and dissipate matter. Containment procedures have been automated and the SCP “Darkhouse” has not been attended to by Foundation personnel since its original containment.


Additional Notes: “It doesn’t shine, it shadows…”

item.title: Uncertain Unreality
item.description: A person, who people think don't exist. Or is it nothing, that makes people think there's a person there?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological… something

Page Layout (Optional): A normal SCP article, but it's split into two distinct sections

Elevator Pitch: The SCP itself is more or less the designation for two separate scenarios. In scenario A, the SCP is a Euclid SCP, who's a young human girl, a bit distorted from reality, and makes half of the people who know of her think she doesn't actually exist.
In scenario B, the SCP is an infohazardous memetic effect, which makes half of the people who know of it think that there's a person there, who really isn't.
The memetic effect of either scenario is so powerful, and so overwhelming, that despite their best efforts, the foundation can't tell which one is true, so they've documented it as if it's neither and both at the same time.
After all, it's impossible to prove either way

Central Narrative: The main narrative is gonna come from how the scenario A SCP is mentally affected by her affliction, and how she may have gotten like this based on interviews with her and the like
Also, it's going to focus on how this uncertainty is affecting the foundation personnel who know of the SCP, including conflicts starting due to people in scenario A starting fights with people in scenario B
People are getting angry about a whole humanoid containment chamber which is going completely unused

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the main hook is obviously the esoterics of something that can't be proven to exist or not exist, and possibly how the foundation reacts to encountering something that they can't truly understand despite their best efforts. I'd imagine people would already be interested as soon as they see "Object Class: Euclid / Keter (?)"

Additional Notes: I guess above all else I want to know if this concept has been done before and if so I would like to know how to make it more unique.
Also, I just wanna know if it's good or not alltogether

item.title: Skeleton's Daycare
item.description: Just a skeleton taking care of some aliens.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: I don't really know, maybe a bit emotional in some parts?

  • Elevator Pitch
  • Central Narrative
  • Hook/Attention Grabber
  • Additional Notes

It's a daycare owned by a living skeleton. The skeleton itself isn't anomalous, it's just a normal human who decomposed into a skeleton but is still alive due to some immortality crystals on the walls of the daycare.

The only other people in the daycare are alien children. For the most part, they're fairly normal. They have a bit of a temper, and they're capable of causing minor earthquakes, so you might not wanna anger them too badly.

This daycare used to be pretty normal. Then these alien parents came in and had to drop their kids off because "they had to do something." When they left the kids at the daycare, they left them with some crystals that would make them and anyone near the crystals immortal.

Two people used to run the daycare, but the original owner left to go find the parents because they've been gone for way too long and they can't close without all the kids leaving. This left the other guy to run it all by himself, but the owner was out for so long that the other guy's body became a skeleton.

After some time, one of the alien parents came back and took their kid, along with one of the crystals. This caused the skeleton's life to become much harder. This, along with the stress of taking care of aliens, was adding up. Then more of the alien parents came in to take their kid and their crystal. It got worse and worse.

At some point, the skeleton couldn't take it anymore and just left the building, causing him to die from getting out of range from the crystals. The children were attached to him after living there for a long time, so they tried to bring him inside and get him to live again, but it didn't work. Remember in the Elevator Pitch how the kids could cause minor earthquakes? They're really upset now, and they're causing serious damage to the rest of the world. They tried calming them down, but nothing would work. Because of the danger, they had to put them into a comatose state and look for their parents quickly. It then ends with the Foundation contacting the original owner who explains that the rest of the parents are long gone. Neutralization was the only other option.

A daycare slowly going into ruins.

None.

item.title: Please don't stare
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, History.

Page Layout (Optional): Probably a good chunk of the article will be filled with dialogues.

Elevator Pitch: a humanoid SCP cursed with a deadly beauty: anyone that makes eye contact cannot feel happiness after that, slowly losing the will to live. The physical aspect of the SCP is different for each person.

Central Narrative: This being would be discovered when the suicide rate of a small town began to show astronomic growth. When brought to the foundation site, a scientist would open the eyes and bring a curse to 5 foundation personnel. The SCP would cooperate with the foundation to try and find a solution, but no amnestics would work and the five would eventually die of starvation or commit suicide, leaving the SCP crying on the corner of it’s cell. Following this tragic event, a series of cold-hearted tests would be performed, including sending many D-class personnel to stare at it’s eyes. The O-5 council decided to shut down the tests for being “too cruel” and the tests would now only be performed in case of someone accidentally staring the creature.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Testing on the SCP would show superhuman strength and resistance, as well as high knowledge in diverse areas and an extensive vocabulary, including many different languages. The SCP would have its own personality, portrayed by the “logs” of his conversation between the scientists, and it loves someone to read a book to it. This SCP is a pacifist, knocking out the opponents instead of killing them (this would be proven in the few containment breaches of his).

Additional Notes: I hadn’t come with a cool name yet. Also, if anyone finds an existing SCP with a similar concept, please notify.

item.title: True NPC
item.description: Self aware NPC attempts to break out to the real world
item.content:encoded:

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): (meta) Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Two variants of the article, one describing the SCP upon discovery and initial tests, the other after learning about it's true scope and it's attempts to escape

Elevator Pitch: Self aware NPC attempts to break out to the real world, after Foundation tries to contain it, and learns about multi-layered nature of the Foundation reality, created specifically to stop pataphysical threats

Central Narrative: Foundation learns about the existence of a self aware character from roleplaying games, whose name is a cognitohazard, that forces people perceiving it to include this character in their roleplaying activities. They try to contain it, like any other memetically spreading SCP, but it did not want to have its freedom restricted, so it decided to break out to the real world. Foundation, prepared for this kind of pataphysical dangers, created beforehand many layers of fictional realities, each identical to the top one, with Earth, Foundation and all the jazz, to contain entities traveling upwards through layers of fictional realities.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Afaik there are no skips going "upwards'' through the reality layers, besides SCP-3812, who accidently went from our reality one level higher, but we don't have any coming from "below" and on purpose. Similarly, there is a multitude of fictional (from the in-universe point of view) SCPs but not much connected to the roleplaying (books and computer games get the majority of attention in this area afaik). I'm also planning on exploring limits of the mentioned cognitohazard, and the entity itself through test logs (something I see rather rarely, but find personally fascinating).

Additional Notes: English is not my first language (as you can probably tell) and I'll be thankful for pointing any misspellings or grammar mistakes. Also I never before used any »real« internet forum more complicated than facebook or reddit, so I'm sorry in advance for my mistakes while trying to make sense of it (I hope that I created this post in the right way). Thanks for reading, I hope you will like my idea, and maybe I'll manage to get the greenlight for my first SCP ^^


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
I'll make sure to remember it for the next time ~Mic4u

item.title: A Simple Bar
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Interview logs and also a log about when the bar manifested and when the Foundation sent an MTF in to determine if the place is a threat

Elevator Pitch: A "simple" bar and owner of said bar, that has the ability to hop across dimensions in order to serve as many customers as possible. Said bar
sets up shop just outside a Foundation site in the middle of nowhere in the hopes of making more money.

Central Narrative:
+Block
-Block

The bartender and owner is relatively open and talkative about the people he's met and places he's been, but when the foundation start trying to find out
some of the more personal questions about his and the bars history he starts getting more dismissive and less talkative. My idea is that the Owner used to run the place with his brother until they traveled to a dimension they weren't welcome in, with the consequence being that the brother is kept half dead, bloody, and basically soulless chained up in the back room of the bar. The owner is unable to let his brother die and let himself move on, so he pays the strange man who lives in the dimension a fee every month for him to help keep his brother alive. In an attempt to make as much money as he can to pay the strangers increasing demands he puts his bar down next to a very busy Foundation site. The interviews with foundation staff start fine with the owner happily telling stories and chatting, but each interview he gets more and more reserved and disturbed with hints and clues as to his brothers fate, until just before an interview the owner comes out from the backroom with blood on his hands with tears in his eyes.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What I'm trying to go for is it starting all happy with stories and fun banter and slowly see it turn into horror.

Additional Notes: I plan on leaving most of the history of the place only hinted at so the reader could speculate and come to their own conclusions.
